issues.legal_issue: A later notification identifying areas covered by an existing royalty-rate notification applies the previously prescribed rate from the earlier notification’s effective date when it merely clarifies which areas fall within that rate.
material_facts: An earlier notification prescribed an increased royalty rate and made it effective from a stated date, while providing that the areas in which the relevant minerals occurred would be identified separately.
A later notification identified the relevant areas and referred to the rate already prescribed by the earlier notification.
The lessee extracted the relevant minerals from an identified area, and the royalty demand related to extraction from the earlier notification’s effective date.
The lessee did not challenge the validity or effective date of the earlier notification.
issues.conclusion: The later notification was clarificatory, so the increased royalty was payable from the effective date specified in the earlier notification, not merely from the date of the later notification.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rule 26(1), (4) and (5) of the Bihar Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1972, royalty is charged at the scheduled rate, and a notified change to the schedules operates from the date specified for it. A legal instrument that is clarificatory, declaratory or explanatory, and supplies an omission or resolves doubt about an existing law, is generally retrospective. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income Tax-I, Ahmedabad v. Gold Coin Health Food Pvt. Ltd. and Zile Singh v. State of Haryana. Although delegated legislation cannot impose retrospective obligations without authority from the parent statute, that principle did not prevent retrospective operation here because the later notification clarified the earlier rate notification rather than creating a new liability.

rule.if: royalty_demand_dispute and earlier_notice_set_rate_effective_start and earlier_notice_required_separate_area_identification and later_notice_identified_qualifying_areas and later_notice_referred_to_existing_rate and extracted_materials_fell_within_the_rate_category

predicates.royalty_demand_dispute: A dispute concerns a demand for royalty on minerals extracted under a lease.
predicates.earlier_notice_set_rate_effective_start: An earlier notice prescribed a royalty rate and stated when that rate would take effect.
predicates.earlier_notice_required_separate_area_id: The earlier notice provided that the areas covered by the rate would be identified separately.
predicates.later_notice_identified_qualifying_areas: A later notice identified areas as falling within the earlier notice’s mineral category.
predicates.later_notice_referred_to_existing_rate: The later notice referred to the rate already prescribed by the earlier notice rather than prescribing a different rate.
predicates.extracted_materials_fell_within_the_rate: The lessee extracted materials that fell within the mineral category covered by the prescribed rate.
predicates.higher_royalty_applies_from_the_earlier_: The increased royalty is payable from the effective start stated in the earlier notice.

issues.definition: When a royalty demand concerns minerals covered by an earlier rate notice that requires separate identification of qualifying areas, and a later notice identifies those areas by reference to the existing rate, the increased royalty applies from the earlier effective start.

issues.legal_issue: Minerals described in a later notification as fit and suitable for making chips fall within a royalty category covering minerals used for making chips when the materials are capable of being used for that purpose.
material_facts: The scheduled royalty category covered boulder, gravel and shingle used for making chips.
The later notification identified boulder, gravel and shingle in specified areas as fit and suitable for making stone chips.
The lessee acknowledged dealing in boulder, gravel and shingle used for making chips.
issues.conclusion: The later notification did not alter the description of the minerals; the category included minerals used, or capable of being used, for making chips.
issues.legal_principle: The Court read the two notifications together with Rule 26 of the Bihar Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1972, including the note requiring separate identification of areas. It interpreted the later notification’s description of materials as fit and suitable for making chips as identifying materials within the existing category, not as changing that category. The Court also treated the later notification as clarificatory, applying the principles stated in Commissioner of Income Tax-I, Ahmedabad v. Gold Coin Health Food Pvt. Ltd. and Zile Singh v. State of Haryana.

predicates.royalty_category_dispute: A dispute concerns whether extracted minerals fall within a category attracting a specified royalty rate.
predicates.existing_category_covers_materials_used_: The existing category describes minerals used for a particular processing purpose.
predicates.later_notice_described_materials_as_suit: A later notice described minerals in identified areas as fit or suitable for that processing purpose.
predicates.extracted_materials_were_of_that_kind: The lessee extracted minerals of the kind described in the notices.
predicates.capable_materials_fall_within_the_existi: Minerals capable of being used for the stated processing purpose fall within the existing royalty category.

issues.definition: When an existing royalty category covers materials used for a purpose and a later notice describes the extracted kind as suitable for that purpose, those materials fall within the category.
